quotes/kierkegaard-leap-para/text: Kierkegaard’s Climacus argues that faith cannot rest on historical scholarship or speculative proof, which can only yield approximation; it is the passionate, inward appropriation of an objective uncertainty — the absolute paradox of the eternal God in time — and so requires a “leap”.
quotes/vatican-i-natural-light/text: The same Holy Mother Church holds and teaches that God, the beginning and end of all things, may be certainly known by the natural light of human reason, by means of created things.
quotes/brunner-contact-para/text: Brunner argues that though the material image of God was lost in the fall, a formal image remains — humans are still responsible, addressable beings — so there is a “point of contact” for the gospel and a real, if insufficient, revelation of God in creation.
quotes/barth-nein-para/text: Barth replies with an unconditional “No”: there is no point of contact in humanity independent of grace and no revelation in nature to be combined with revelation in Christ; such natural theology, he warns, is the door through which the “German Christians” brought nation and race into the church.
quotes/lewis-trilemma-para/text: Lewis argues that a man who said what Jesus said would not be a great moral teacher: he would be a lunatic or something worse, unless he was who he claimed to be; we must choose, and patronising talk of Jesus as merely a good teacher is not open to us.
quotes/van-til-presupposition-para/text: Van Til argues that there is no neutral ground between belief and unbelief: the unbeliever borrows the order, logic and morality that only the God of Scripture can ground, so the apologist should show that the Christian worldview is the precondition of intelligibility.
quotes/dei-verbum-para/text: Vatican II teaches that God has revealed himself and his will fully in Christ, so that no new public revelation is to be expected before the Lord’s return; it also repeats that God can be known from created things by the light of reason.
quotes/craig-kalam-para/text: Craig’s kalām argument: whatever begins to exist has a cause; the universe began to exist (shown philosophically and by big-bang cosmology); therefore the universe has a cause, which must be a personal, timeless and immensely powerful Creator.
quotes/swinburne-cumulative-para/text: Swinburne argues that while no single argument proves God, the existence of the universe, its law-like order, fine-tuning, consciousness, moral awareness, miracles and religious experience together make theism more probable than not.
quotes/plantinga-properly-basic-para/tex: Plantinga argues that belief in God, like belief in other minds or in the past, can be “properly basic” — rational without being inferred from evidence — when produced by a properly functioning faculty such as Calvin’s sense of the divine.
quotes/plantinga-free-will-defence-para/: Plantinga argues that it is possible that God could not create a world containing free creatures who always choose rightly, so the existence of God and of evil is not logically contradictory.
quotes/augustine-give-what-thou-commande: Give what Thou commandest, and command what Thou wilt.
quotes/augustine-restless-heart/text: Thou hast formed us for Thyself, and our hearts are restless till they find rest in Thee.
quotes/augustine-evil-use-of-free-will/t: For it was by the evil use of his free-will that man destroyed both it and himself.
quotes/augustine-nature-wounded/text: Human nature was created without fault, but in Adam it was wounded; the grace of Christ is therefore not only a law or a teaching laid before us but a healing medicine that sets the will free to love what it commands.
quotes/augustine-city-of-god-eternal/tex: Augustine argues that "eternal" in Matthew 25:46 must mean the same for punishment as for life, so that the hope of "the merciful" for an end to the torments of the damned cannot stand.
quotes/pelagius-demetrias-capacity/text: Pelagius tells Demetrias that before urging holiness he must first show the strength and quality of human nature: God, who is just, never commands the impossible, and the good of nature is proved even among the pagans.
quotes/cassian-will-begins/text: Cassian teaches that God sometimes anticipates the will and sometimes waits for it, so that when he sees in us the beginnings of a good will he at once enlightens, strengthens and urges it on to salvation.
quotes/caesarius-orange-conclusion/text: The council concludes that through the sin of the first man free will was so weakened that no one can love God, believe, or do good for God’s sake unless grace has gone before; and it anathematises any who say that some are predestined to evil by divine power.
quotes/gottschalk-twofold/text: Gottschalk confesses that God by an unchangeable decree has predestined the elect to eternal life and the reprobate to eternal death — a single predestination that is "twofold" (gemina).
quotes/aquinas-grace-perfects-nature/tex: Since therefore grace does not destroy nature but perfects it, natural reason should minister to faith.
quotes/aquinas-grace-moves-will/text: Aquinas teaches that a person cannot prepare himself for grace without the gratuitous help of God moving him inwardly, and that merit itself is the fruit of grace, since God crowns his own gifts.
quotes/molina-middle-knowledge/text: Molina argues that God knows, prior to his decree, what every possible free creature would freely do in every possible circumstance; by choosing which circumstances to actualise, God providentially ordains all things without overriding freedom.
quotes/pascal-two-graces/text: Pascal mocks a "sufficient grace" that does not suffice, defending against the Jesuit casuists the Augustinian teaching that efficacious grace infallibly and yet sweetly moves the will.
quotes/luther-free-lord-servant/text: A Christian man is the most free lord of all, and subject to none; a Christian man is the most dutiful servant of all, and subject to every one.
quotes/luther-joyful-exchange/text: Faith unites the soul to Christ as a bride to her bridegroom: all that Christ has — grace, life, righteousness — becomes the soul’s, and all that the soul has — sin, death, damnation — becomes Christ’s.
quotes/luther-bound-will/text: Against Erasmus, Luther likens the human will to a beast of burden standing between two riders: ridden by God it goes where God wills, ridden by Satan where Satan wills, and it cannot choose its rider.
quotes/luther-smalcald-chief-article/tex: Of this article nothing can be yielded or surrendered, even though heaven and earth, and whatever will not abide, should sink to ruin.
quotes/melanchthon-augsburg-iv/text: Also they teach that men cannot be justified before God by their own strength, merits, or works, but are freely justified for Christ’s sake, through faith, when they believe that they are received into favor, and that their sins are forgiven for Christ’s sake, who, by His death, has made satisfaction for our sins.
quotes/calvin-without-christ/text: So long as we are without Christ and separated from him, nothing which he suffered and did for the salvation of the human race is of the least benefit to us.
quotes/calvin-principal-hinge/text: The principal hinge by which religion is supported.
quotes/calvin-predestination-defined/tex: By predestination we mean the eternal decree of God, by which he determined with himself whatever he wished to happen with regard to every man. All are not created on equal terms, but some are preordained to eternal life, others to eternal damnation.
quotes/calvin-mystical-union/text: Calvin insists that we do not contemplate Christ at a distance so that his righteousness is imputed to us from outside; rather, because we have put on Christ and been grafted into his body, he deigns to make us one with himself — the "mystical union" he ranks of the highest importance.
quotes/arminius-grace-resistible/text: Arminius declares that he ascribes to grace the beginning, continuation and completion of all good, so that even the regenerate can neither think nor do good without it; the only question is whether grace is an irresistible force — and he believes Scripture shows many who resisted the Holy Spirit.
quotes/spurgeon-calvinism-gospel/text: It is a nickname to call it Calvinism; Calvinism is the gospel, and nothing else.
quotes/wesley-heart-strangely-warmed/tex: I felt my heart strangely warmed. I felt I did trust in Christ, Christ alone, for salvation; and an assurance was given me that He had taken away my sins, even mine, and saved me from the law of sin and death.
quotes/wesley-perfect-love/text: Wesley explains Christian perfection as nothing higher or lower than pure love filling the heart and governing words and actions — not freedom from ignorance, mistakes or temptation, and never a state beyond growth or beyond need of Christ.
quotes/palmer-altar/text: Phoebe Palmer taught a "shorter way": lay all on the altar, which is Christ, believe God’s promise that the altar sanctifies the gift, and testify to entire sanctification now rather than waiting for feelings.
quotes/smith-rest-of-faith/text: Hannah Whitall Smith urges believers to stop striving and to hand over the whole of life to Christ in full consecration, trusting him moment by moment to live the victorious life in them.
quotes/durham-finished-work/text: Durham argued that the believer is sanctified in Christ at conversion by the finished work of Calvary; there is no second crisis of cleansing, only an ongoing appropriation of what was already given.
quotes/hodges-free-grace/text: Hodges holds that eternal life is given freely to anyone who believes Jesus’ promise of it; to require surrender, perseverance or fruit as conditions of salvation or of assurance would turn grace into a reward.
quotes/macarthur-lordship/text: MacArthur argues that the gospel Jesus preached calls sinners to repentance and to submit to him as Lord; a "faith" that leaves life unchanged is not the saving faith of the New Testament.
quotes/sanders-covenantal-nomism/text: Sanders argues that in Palestinian Judaism one "gets in" to the covenant by God’s gracious election and "stays in" by obedience and atonement — a pattern he calls covenantal nomism, not legalistic earning of salvation.
quotes/wright-justification-covenant/tex: Wright argues that for Paul justification is God’s declaration of who belongs to his single worldwide covenant family, marked by faith in Jesus, anticipating the final verdict that will accord with the whole life lived in the Spirit.
quotes/athanasius-made-god/text: For He was made man that we might be made God; and He manifested Himself by a body that we might receive the idea of the unseen Father; and He endured the insolence of men that we might inherit immortality.
quotes/irenaeus-become-what-we-are/text: Our Lord Jesus Christ, who did, through His transcendent love, become what we are, that He might bring us to be even what He is Himself.
quotes/irenaeus-glory-living-man/text: For the glory of God is a living man; and the life of man consists in beholding God.
quotes/palamas-energies/text: Palamas teaches that God is wholly present in his uncreated energies, so that the saints truly participate in God and become gods by grace, while God’s essence remains utterly beyond participation and knowledge.
quotes/origen-end-like-beginning/text: For the end is always like the beginning.
quotes/origen-enemies-subdued/text: Origen reasons from 1 Corinthians 15:24-28 that when Christ subjects all things to the Father, his enemies are conquered not by destruction but by correction, so that God may be "all in all".
